articles.title: Paratleta denuncia capacitismo após ser questionado sobre deficiência | G1
articles.standfirst: João Fontenelle, de 26 anos, afirma que funcionário da Latam exigiu laudo médico durante embarque e disse que ele 'não parecia ter deficiência'. Atleta disputa campeonato em São Paulo.
articles.summary: João Fontenelle afirma que funcionário da Latam exigiu laudo médico durante embarque e disse que ele 'não parecia ter deficiência'. Atleta disputa campeonato em São Paulo.
articles.body:
O paratleta acreano João Fernando Fontenelle, de 26 anos, afirma ter sido vítima de capacitismo após ter a deficiência questionada ao embarcar em um voo da Latam Airlines, na madrugada dessa terça-feira (10), no Aeroporto Internacional de Rio Branco .

Ao g1 , o atleta, que é atual recordista brasileiro no arremesso de peso , contou que um funcionário da companhia exigiu a apresentação de um laudo médico na fila preferencial do check-in e afirmou que ele 'não parecia ser uma pessoa com deficiência'. Ele nasceu com pé cavo bilateral, uma condição que afeta os dois pés.

"Eu falei que tinha um laudo, mas nunca tinham me perguntado sobre isso. Ele começou a me olhar de cima a baixo, como se eu estivesse mentindo. Meu professor, que já tinha passado, precisou avisar que eu estava com a equipe. Foi quando ele me deixou passar", relata.

Em nota, a Latam disse que repudia veementemente qualquer tipo de ofensa ou prática discriminatória e que atitudes contrárias a esse princípio não refletem seus valores. "A Latam está analisando o caso com a devida seriedade", informou o texto. (Veja a nota completa mais abaixo)

João Fernando Fontenelle denunciou ter sido vítima de capacitismo por um funcionário da Latam Airlines — Foto: Arquivo pessoal

Mesmo depois de conseguir autorização para seguir, João disse que foi novamente abordado pelo funcionário. "Ele falou: 'Mas é porque tu não tem cara de quem tem deficiência'. Eu respondi que era deficiente, sim. Depois de tudo caiu a ficha que fui vítima de capacitismo ", conta.

Além do treinador, João estava acompanhado de outros dois atletas. O grupo utilizava a fila de embarque preferencial para viajar a São Paulo , onde o acreano participa do Campeonato Brasileiro de Atletismo Paralímpico, entre esta quinta-feira (12) e sábado (14) no Estádio do Ibirapuera.

João afirma ainda que por conta da pressa para embarcar e o medo de perder o voo acabou ficando sem reação no momento da abordagem.

"Não foi nem o jeito de perguntar, mas a forma como ele me tratou, como se eu estivesse mentindo. Fiquei em choque e as pessoas ficaram me olhando, isso foi muito constrangedor", diz.

A Associação Paradesportiva Acreana publicou uma nota em repúdio ao caso e em defesa do paratleta. "Nosso atleta não estava pedindo favor. Estava exercendo seu direito de ir e vir, de representar o Acre com dignidade e orgulho. Ele superou barreiras que muitos nem imaginam, para chegar onde chegou", criticou.

João viajava para São Paulo para disputar o Campeonato Brasileiro de Atletismo Paralímpico — Foto: Ingrid Maia/Arquivo pessoal

A LATAM Airlines Brasil informa que está analisando o caso com a devida seriedade. Os procedimentos da LATAM sempre objetivam o cumprimento da regulamentação vigente e eventuais desvios serão utilizados para reforço e reorientação junto às equipes visando garantir um atendimento respeitoso, inclusivo e acessível a todos os passageiros.

A companhia reitera que repudia veementemente qualquer tipo de ofensa ou prática discriminatória e que atitudes contrárias a esse princípio não refletem seus valores.

A ASSOCIAÇÃO PARADESPORTIVA ACREANA vem a público manifestar TOTAL REPÚDIO ao ato de discriminação sofrido por nosso atleta paralímpico, integrante da Delegação Acreana, por um atendente da companhia aérea LATAM.

Mesmo estando devidamente fardado, identificado e junto à sua delegação, nosso atleta foi constrangido e teve sua deficiência questionada pelo atendente, sob a justificativa de que sua deficiência “não era visível”.

Nem toda deficiência é visível. Existem deficiências intelectuais, auditivas, orgânicas, doenças raras, autismo, entre tantas outras que não estão estampadas no rosto. Questionar, duvidar e humilhar uma pessoa por isso é capacitismo, é violência e é crime.

Nosso atleta não estava pedindo favor. Estava exercendo seu direito de ir e vir, de representar nosso Estado, com dignidade e orgulho. Ele treinou, se dedicou, superou barreiras que muitos nem imaginam, para chegar onde chegou.

Apuração rigorosa do ocorrido e responsabilização do funcionário envolvido;

Capacitação URGENTE de todos os seus atendentes sobre os direitos das Pessoas com Deficiência, deficiência invisível e atendimento humanizado;

Garantia de que nenhum outro atleta ou PCD passe por isso novamente

A Lei Brasileira de Inclusão (Lei 13.146/2015) garante atendimento prioritário e sem discriminação. O que aconteceu fere a lei, fere a dignidade humana e fere todo o movimento paralímpico. Ao nosso atleta: você é nosso orgulho! Não é você quem deve se envergonhar. Quem deve se envergonhar é quem ainda julga um corpo pela aparência. Estamos com você. Não vamos nos calar!

articles.title: ‘I feel I have won the Olympic gold once again’: MM Somaya gets medal back as Bengaluru Police crack theft case
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Former India hockey captain MM Somaya has got back his prized 1980 Moscow Olympics gold medal after Bengaluru Police cracked the theft case and
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Former India hockey captain MM Somaya has got back his prized 1980 Moscow Olympics gold medal after Bengaluru Police cracked the theft case and recovered the stolen medals and other valuables from his residence. Two people have been arrested in connection with the incident, bringing relief to the three-time Olympian, who described the recovery as an emotional moment.Expressing gratitude to the police for their efforts, Somaya said their reassurance throughout the investigation had helped him remain hopeful that the medals would be recovered."I am extremely grateful to the Bangalore Police, headed by Mr Seemant (Kumar Singh), who have worked really hard over the last few days. They have not been able to recover only the medal, but also some valuables stolen from my residence," Somaya told reporters.He also acknowledged the efforts of DCP East Dr Vikram, the ACP of Halsur, police inspector Anand and the Indiranagar police team, who had assured him from the beginning that the medals would be traced."They are an honor not only for me personally but it is an honor for the state and the country. So he was very reassuring and he and his team at the Indiranagar Police station have done a magnificent job. And I'm really grateful to them. I feel I have won the Olympic medal once again. I am really happy with how police handled this case and cracked within a short period," he added.Two arrested, all stolen medals and valuables recoveredBengaluru Police Commissioner Seemant Kumar Singh said the police had recovered all the stolen medals and valuables and handed them back to Somaya after completing the legal formalities."This case of the theft which was reported in Indira Nagar police station by Mr Somaiya about the theft of gold medal and silver medals which he had won so in such a great manner for the pride of the country. So today we are happy that my entire team could detect that case, two people have been arrested and all the valuables as well as all the medals which were stolen have been recovered and we deem it our privilege to have handed over all the medals to Mr Somaiya as per legal formalities after being completed," he told ANI.Singh described the investigation as one of the most challenging cases for the police because there were no initial clues. He said the two arrested accused had been involved in similar crimes earlier and that the police would ensure they did not repeat such offences."This is reassuring for us, motivating for us, especially for our lower forces who keep working day and night and this was one of the most challenging cases for us because we didn't have any clue for it. So finally we could detect this case and recover the items and those two people who are there, they are the accused who have been caught are people who have been involved in such crimes earlier also. We will see to it that in future they do not do such an act," he added.Somaya recalls shock of theft, emotional value of Olympic goldThe theft took place on October 28, when Somaya and his family were away on a short holiday in Coorg, his native place. After being alerted by a neighbour, they rushed back to Bengaluru and registered a complaint, with an FIR filed on the same day."Actually we had gone to Coorg (at the time of theft), my native place, for a short holiday and this happened by the thieves breaking into the house which was really a shock for us. Fortunately we were alerted quickly by one of our neighbours and we rushed back from Coorg and were able to register our complaint and also the FIR was filed on the same day," Somaya said.The 1980 Olympic gold holds special significance for Somaya, who also represented India at the 1984 Los Angeles and 1988 Seoul Olympics, captaining the side at the latter. He won silver at the 1982 Asian Games in Delhi and bronze at the 1986 edition in Seoul.Recalling the amateur era of Indian hockey, Somaya explained why the medals meant far more to him than their material value."It (the medals) are many years of work and in those days there was no monetary awards, it was an amateur sport so the medals are a little bit of an honour actually and not only for me but for the state and the country. So I carry a lot of memories and sentiments so it is very special to me, especially the Olympic gold medal and I am really happy that they are back with me now," he said.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: La mayor leyenda del olimpismo sudafricano anuncia entre lágrimas que cambia de país
articles.standfirst: La bracista Tatjana Smith, doble oro olímpico, nadará ahora representando a Países Bajos
articles.summary: La bracista Tatjana Smith, doble oro olímpico, nadará ahora representando a Países Bajos
articles.body: La cuádruple medallista olímpica Tatjana Smith (de soltera Schoenmaker) no pudo contener las lágrimas. La bracista anunciaba mediante un vídeo en las redes sociales que dejaba de representar a Sudáfrica, su país de nacimiento, para abrazar la bandera neerlandesa, la tierra de sus ancestros, en una decisión motivada por cuestiones económicas. Tatjana Smith gano dos oros -uno de ellos con récord mundial incluido- y dos platas entre Tokio 2020 y París 2024 en los 100 y 200 braza, un botín del que no puede presumir ningún otro deportista sudafricano en la historia de los Juegos Olímpicos, ni siquiera el gran Chad le Clos. A sus 29 años, Smith tiene la mira puesta en Los Ángeles 2028. “Representar a Sudáfrica en los Juegos Olímpicos era mi mayor sueño de infancia. Haberlo vivido y ganado cuatro medallas olímpicas es algo que siempre atesoraré”, dijo Smith en el emotivo vídeo. “Sudáfrica y los Países Bajos siempre han formado parte de mi identidad. Estoy profundamente agradecida a la comunidad de natación sudafricana, a todos mis entrenadores y a todos los sudafricanos que me animaron. Esa gratitud jamás cambiará”, aseguró la bracista, que seguirá entrenando en Sudáfrica con su técnico de toda la vida. “Mi carrera como nadadora puede que tome un rumbo diferente, pero mi conexión con Sudáfrica nunca cambiará. Elegir un nuevo camino no borra el viaje que me trajo hasta aquí. Simplemente me da la oportunidad de escribir un nuevo capítulo”, explicó Smith con el corazón encogido. Tatjana llevaba tiempo criticando a la Swimming South Africa (SSA) e incluso envió una carta a la organización en relación con la retención de los premios en metálico en 2023. Según la nadadora, la federación sudafricana lleva mucho tiempo sin priorizar a los nadadores, y denuncia la falta de apoyo financiero. Smith se había retirado previamente de la natación competitiva tras los Juegos Olímpicos de París 2024, pero en septiembre anunció que regresaría en busca de una tercera participación olímpica. "Representar a Países Bajos le brinda a Smith la oportunidad de explorar sus raíces neerlandesas a través del deporte y experimentar un enfoque diferente del entrenamiento de alto rendimiento", declaró su equipo en un comunicado de prensa que anunciaba el cambio. "La estructura de apoyo disponible le permitirá dedicarse por completo a su rendimiento y construir una carrera de natación más sostenible", añadió, dejando claro que el apoyo económico que le brinda la federación neerlandesa ha sido clave a la hora de tomar esta difícil decisión. Smith ya compitió en el Campeonato Holandés de Natación a finales de octubre en Rotterdam, arrasando en las pruebas de braza con tiempos de 29.54 en los 50 metros, 1:03.92 en los 100 metros y 2:19.96 en los 200 metros. Smith representará a los Países Bajos por primera vez a nivel internacional en el Campeonato Mundial de Piscina Corta de 2026, que tendrá lugar dentro de tres semanas en Pekín.

images.caption: Tatjana Smith celebra tras ganar la final de los 100 metros braza en los Juegos Olímpicos de París. LAPRESSE

articles.title: Niraj Kumar scripts history with World Championships bronze, secures LA 2028 Olympic quota
articles.summary: India's shooting contingent has received a major boost ahead of the Los Angeles 2028 Olympics, with Niraj Kumar securing an Olympic quota place after
articles.body: India's shooting contingent has received a major boost ahead of the Los Angeles 2028 Olympics, with Niraj Kumar securing an Olympic quota place after winning bronze in the men's 50m rifle 3 positions event at the ISSF World Championships in Doha, Qatar.The 26-year-old delivered a composed performance in the final on Wednesday, finishing third with 346.5 points to claim his maiden individual medal at the World Championships. The achievement also earned India a quota place for the upcoming Summer Games, taking the country's tally at the competition to two.Dmitrii Pimenov, competing as an Individual Neutral Athlete, won the gold medal, while Slovakia's Patrik Jany settled for silver. Norway's Jon-Hermann Hegg finished fourth and secured the third available Olympic quota in the event, as Jany had already earned one for his country.Niraj Kumar ends wait for maiden individual World Championships medalThe bronze medal marks a significant breakthrough for Niraj, who has consistently featured among India's promising rifle shooters. Despite reaching the final of major international competitions on previous occasions, an individual World Championships medal had remained elusive. His performance in Doha finally brought that long-awaited achievement.Niraj also contributed to India's bronze medal in the men's 50m rifle 3 positions team event alongside Aishwary Pratap Singh Tomar and Akhil Sheoran. The Indian trio finished with a combined score of 1,751 points.Czechia claimed the team gold, while Norway secured silver.India secure second shooting quota for LA 2028 OlympicsNiraj's performance added another Olympic quota to India's shooting tally at the ongoing World Championships. Earlier, Jaypal Malviya had secured India's first quota place after winning silver in the men's 10m air pistol event.The qualification places India in a stronger position as the shooting contingent begins its preparations for the Los Angeles 2028 Olympics. However, the quota place is allocated to India and does not guarantee Niraj an automatic selection for the Games. The final decision on the participating shooter will be taken by the Indian shooting authorities closer to the Olympics.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: María Pérez entra en el 'Top ten' de mejores atletas del año para World Athletics
articles.standfirst: La granadina fue campeona de Europa de medio maratón marcha en Birmingham con un récord mundial
articles.summary: La granadina fue campeona de Europa de medio maratón marcha en Birmingham con un récord mundial
articles.body: María Pérez sigue acaparando reconocimientos. La marchadora granadina, oro en el medio maratón marcha del Europeo de Birmingham el pasado verano, ha sido incluida por World Athletics (WA) en su 'top ten' de mejores atletas femeninas de 2026. La atleta de Orce, novena en esta prestigiosa clasificación, se impuso en la ciudad inglesa con un nuevo récord mundial (1h30:06) en una distancia que sustituye a los tradicionales 20 km marcha. Esto le ha valido para sumar un nuevo éxito tras ganar en 2025 el premio como 'Atleta femenina del año' en la categoría de fuera estadio, un galardón que también concede WA. En el Mundial de Tokio, María defendió con éxito su doblete de Budapest 2023 (oros en los 20 y 35 km marcha), convirtiéndose en la primera mujer en reeditar dos títulos mundiales individuales. Las tres nominadas a 'Atleta femenina del año' son la velocidad estadounidense Melissa Jefferson-Wooden, oro en los 100 y 200 metros del Ultimate Championship; su compatriota Masai Russell, nueva plusmarquista mundial de los 100 vallas, y la suiza Audrey Werro, que ha revolucionado el 800 hasta el punto de poner en jaque el vetusto récord mundial de Jarmila Kratochvílová. Cuarta y quinta son la etíope Tigst Assefa y la dominicana Marileidy Paulino. La primera ganó este año los prestigiosos maratones de Londres y Berlín, donde se quedó cerca de asaltar el récord mundial, mientras que la segunda a vuelto a dominar los 400 metros con mano de hierro. Sexta ha sido la keniana Agnes Ngetich, oro mundial tanto en cross como medio maratón, seguida de la lanzadora de peso estadounidense Chase Jackson, campeona mundial indoor y autora de la segunda mejor marca en lo que va de siglo (21,14 metros) en una prueba marcada como pocas por el antiguo dopaje de los países del Este. Octava ha sido la lanzadora de jabalina china Yan Ziyi, que a sus 18 años se ha situado segunda en el ranking mundial de todos los tiempos con 71.74 metros, sólo superada por la checa Barbora Spotakova. Y tras María, en décima posición, se ha situado otra lanzadora, en este caso de martillo. La canadiense Camryn Rogers, oro olímpico en París, ha afianzado su segundo puesto en la lista histórica de su especialidad con un tiro de 81,13 metros. WA ya anunció ayer los tres finalistas a mejor 'Atleta masculino del año', con el brasileño y nuevo plusmarquista mundial de 400 vallas Alison dos Santos pugnando por el galardón con el pertiguista sueco Armand Duplantis y el maratoniano keniano Sabastian Sawe, que se convirtió en Londres en el primer hombre en romper la barrera de las dos horas en un maratón homologado. Completaron el 'top ten' el británico Josh Kerr, nuevo plusmarquista mundial de la milla; el estadounidense Ja’Kobe Tharp, nuevo plusmarquista mundial de los 110 vallas; el velocista estadounidense Kenneth Bednarek, doble campeón de 100 y 200 metros en el Ultimate Championship; el cuatrocentista botsuano Collen Kebinatshipi, el lanzando de jabalina de Sri Lanka Rumesh Tharanga Pathirage, el triplista italiano Andy Díaz y el lanzador de disco esloveno Kristjan Čeh.

articles.title: El taekwondista Iván Lysenko suma la octava medalla española en Dakar
articles.standfirst: El valenciano, único español en esta disciplina, perdió en la final frente al iraní Benyamin Soltanian
articles.summary: El valenciano, único español en esta disciplina, vence en la final
articles.body: España ha sumado su octava medalla -la novena llegó poco después-, tercera de plata, en los Juegos Olímpicos de la Juventud que se disputan en Dakar (Senegal). El protagonista ha sido el taekwondista valenciano Iván Lysenko, en la categoría de +73 kilos. Lysenko era el único español presente en este deporte y ha firmado una competición casi perfecta. El valenciano, que llegaba a Dakar con la moral reforzada tras ganar el European Grand Prix Open 2026, se imponía en octavos con enorme superioridad al gabonés Claude Boulouchi (16-1 y 12-0) y en cuartos despachaba también por la vía rápida al bielorruso Bahdan Aliyeu (17-2 y 15-0). Ya en semis, pasaba bastantes más apuros frente al ruso Bashir Adzhiev (2-10, 10-10 y 6-2), antes de jugarse el oro con el iraní Benyamin Soltanian, que le derrotaba en otro combate igual de parejo por 15-8 y 4-4. En 65 kilos de boxeo, el gaditano Pablo Souto ganó en las preliminares al jordano Abdallah Toghoz y en cuartos de final al trinitense Makieve Belile, pero el púgil del Puerto de Santa María perdió en semifinales ante el israelí Artur Prohnevsky para conformarse con uno de los dos bronces en juego. El gaditano dio a España su novena medallas en los Juegos.

articles.title: GB and Wales' athlete Josh Griffiths banned after drug test
articles.summary: Great Britain and Wales athlete Josh Griffiths was banned after returning a positive drugs test in May.
articles.body:
A Great Britain and Wales marathon runner, who shocked the elite to win a place at the World Championships, was banned after returning a positive drugs test.

Josh Griffiths, 33, was given a three-month ban by the World Athletics' Athletics Integrity Unit (AIU) after Benzoylecgonine - which is found in the body when it processes cocaine - appeared in his system following May's Belfast City Marathon.

Griffiths, who represented Great Britain at the 2017 and 2022 Worlds and ran for Wales at the 2018 Commonwealth Games, denied ever taking cocaine or any other social drug.

He could not prove how cocaine entered his system, but in their ruling the AIU accepted that any ingestion was both out of competition and "unrelated to sport" as they imposed the ban.

Griffiths' ban ran for three months from the hearing date of 19 June 2026. In addition his race results from the day of the Belfast Marathon - 3 May - until the end of the ban were expunged.

Following the findings, Griffiths accepted the anti-doping rule violation and the sanction.

The Carmarthenshire athlete rose to prominence when he finished as the fastest Briton as a club runner in the 2017 London Marathon, earning him a place in the GB squad for that year's World Championships.

He went on to record an eighth-place finish in London in 2021, having turned professional after the 2017 success.

The AIU said in its report that Griffiths remarked it was "absolutely impossible" when he was told of the initial adverse finding in his sample and that "there must have been a mistake".

Benzoylecgonine, which is found in the body when it processes cocaine, appeared in both samples of his urine provided following the Belfast marathon.

Griffiths provided details of his activities and whereabouts leading up to the 3 May race, as well as his stay at the official race hotel, stressing he did not attend any social events, consume any alcohol and that contact had been mainly with other athletes and race staff.

At a later hearing, he reiterated that he had never knowingly ingested cocaine and was not aware of anyone close to him using the drug in the lead-up to the Belfast race.

Griffiths submitted scientific data to support his claim that any ingestion was out of competition, something the AIU went on to agree with.

articles.title: Lindsey Vonn gives health update as she undergoes ninth surgery following brutal Olympic crash
articles.summary: Lindsey Vonn revealed she's heading into her ninth surgery to remove plates and screws before finally getting a new ACL after her Olympic crash.
articles.body: It's been nearly ten months since Lindsey Vonn sustained brutal injuries in a crash at the 2026 Winter Olympics in Milan, and the skiing star revealed that her recovery is still very much ongoing. The 42-year-old five-time Olympian hopped on social media to inform her followers that she had gone in for surgery. For the ninth time. LINDSEY VONN ALL SMILES AS SHE'S ABLE TO RETURN TO DUMPING OUT ACTUAL WORKOUT CONTENT AGAIN "This will be my ninth surgery," Vonn said in the video. 'I'm doing this beforehand because I'm actually getting pretty nervous about it. On the day of, I'm going to be focused and rested and trying to get through it." Vonn explained that the reason for this surgery was to remove hardware that had been installed during previous procedures. "Basically, what we're doing is removing all of the plates and screws and just basically removing all the hardware to make room for the new ACL because I don't have an ACL still because of all the plates; just couldn't put it in," she explained. Back in February, she was competing on a torn ACL in her left leg that she injured just before the start of the games. She tried to compete in the Olympics, but crashed in the women's downhill event and severely injured the same leg. LINDSEY VONN KEEPS THE BIRTHDAY CELEBRATION GOING, SLIPPING INTO A BODYSUIT FOR CLOTHING LINE'S NEW COLLECTION However, once she has that fresh ACL, she still has a long road ahead of her. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP "So I've been waiting all these nine months so my bones could heal and we could fix the ACL, and my bones healed, which is great news," she said. "But obviously now I have the ACL, and that means another six-to-nine months." Fortunately, Vonn posted on her Instagram story that the surgery went well. She also showed off a big with the hardware that used to be in her left leg captioned, "Got all this s--t out of my leg."

articles.title: A week without end for PT Usha: How a quiet rebellion derailed IOA president's second-term ambitions
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: PT Usha's second-term bid as Indian Olympic Association (IOA) president unravelled in 11 days, as a campaign for change within and outside the
articles.body: NEW DELHI: PT Usha's second-term bid as Indian Olympic Association (IOA) president unravelled in 11 days, as a campaign for change within and outside the IOA gathered pace during her absence while she was in Dakar for the Youth Olympic Games (YOG), according to people familiar with developments. The week began on October 29. Usha met two influential political figures in Delhi, seeking their assurance and blessings for another term, sources said. At 7.09 pm, she filed her nomination for the Sportsperson of Outstanding Merit (SOM) election. That evening, she flew to Dakar for the YOG as part of the Indian delegation, with key office staff.After her departure, sources familiar with back-channel discussions alleged that those seeking a leadership change became active. Several calls, meetings in and outside Delhi and private message exchanges followed. As nominations deadline of Oct 30 passed, Usha's camp sensed alignments were shifting.The draft list, released the next day, deepened the unease. Usha was reportedly alerted in Dakar to a possible rebellion against her presidency. People close to her camp acknowledge that opposition had been building privately for four to five months. They say she was caught off guard and underestimated the challenge. Usha had planned to return on Nov 7. Developments prompted her to cut short the visit, sources said. Two scheduled International Olympic Committee (IOC) engagements kept her in the Senegal capital until Nov 2: a breakfast meeting with IOC vice-president Nawal El Moutawakel and four other delegates, followed by talks with IOC president Kirsty Coventry. They discussed India's 2036 Olympics bid and prospects of hosting the 2038 Asian Games. After the meetings, Usha booked a Nov 3 flight home, reached Delhi on Nov 4 morning and by noon, was present at the IOA office meeting with key aides. By then, mass withdrawals and changing positions among prospective SOM candidates had made her re-election prospects look uncertain, sources said.Sources alleged influential figures urged Usha to withdraw from the SOM contest. She declined, relying on assurances she believed she had received from her political bosses. She eventually lost by finishing fifth with 40 votes in a six-woman contest, possibly ending her bid for a second term as IOA president. Her backers concede she needed to be more proactive: the challenge had been taking shape while she was away. However, Usha separately wrote to electoral officer Sanjay K Srivastava to question an inclusion on the final SOM roster, allegedly of female SOM candidate Dola Banerjee's brother Rahul citing conflict of interest. It sought scrutiny of eligibility and inclusion or exclusion decisions, asking who authorised the inclusion of Rahul, under which rule and on what documentary basis, and whether a conflict of interest had been disclosed by Dola.Usha also filed four complaints with the electoral officer, in possession of TOI. They raised concerns over alleged requests for voters to confirm participation or provide proof of votes; messages invoking the sports ministry to seek voter confirmations; and WhatsApp appeals for a panel and four candidates, allegedly circulated by incumbent IOA executive committee members. She sought inquiry under Model Code of Conduct and ballot secrecy. Sources informed that Usha received no response from Srivastava till date.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: 'If Neeraj Chopra can, why can't I?': National record holder Nirbhay Chaudhary on his Olympic dream
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: \"Maine waha se start kiya hai jaha se log finish karte hain [I have started where others finish]\" - that is how hammer thrower Nirbhay
articles.body: NEW DELHI: "Maine waha se start kiya hai jaha se log finish karte hain [I have started where others finish]" - that is how hammer thrower Nirbhay Chaudhary looks at his national record-breaking performance. He threw 71.02m at the Indian Athletics Series Final this October, breaking a national record that had stood for almost 10 years.His throw erased the previous record of 70.73m, set by Neeraj Kumar in 2016.Despite the record, Nirbhay was not fully satisfied with his effort. After releasing the hammer, he initially thought of stepping out of the circle so that the throw would not be counted. However, he changed his mind.A few moments later, he heard the noise around him. When he asked his coach what had happened, he was told that he had broken the national record."I had made that throw casually. I did not think it would be a record-breaking effort. I had not even used much power. I never expected the hammer to travel so far or that I would break the national record. I don't know how it went that far," Nirbhay told TimesofIndia.com in an exclusive interview.For Nirbhay, whose name means 'fearless', the national record is only the beginning. He now wants to cross 75m and eventually reach the 80m mark."This is just the beginning. I am really proud of this performance. It has given me a new beginning. I have started where others finish," he said.The wall of inspiration: From 70m + to 75mA few months ago, Nirbhay returned to his room after a tiring practice session. He was covered in sweat, but the session had not gone as planned. He was struggling to perform, and his body was getting tired quickly as he recovered from dengue.His family was also worried about his future in athletics. Frustrated and angry, Nirbhay picked up a marker and wrote a target on the wall beside his bed: "70 + national record". He also set a deadline for himself - September 10. He then prepared a training schedule and followed it closely. His routine included waking up early, cleaning his hammer, stretching, working out, running and practising his throws with full power.He achieved his target on the date he had set. After breaking the national record, he crossed out 70m on the wall and replaced it with 75m."I have crossed out 70 and written 75. I will achieve that target too. It is true that there is no substitute for hard work. I believe in that. I am also stubborn. When I work hard with determination, I get what I want. I will continue to do that," Nirbhay said.He revealed that he had written the target on the wall last year, when he was going through a difficult phase."I had written it last year. I was very frustrated at that time. My family was also worried because my physical condition had become very poor. Everyone was asking me to continue with the sport, even if I could only do a little."I know what condition I was in. And it has taken a year for this to happen. But the happiness I feel now cannot be bought. The feeling is surreal. But I won't stop," he said.Nirbhay believes one more season of hard work can help him make a big jump in his performance."I just need one more season. I can achieve a big mark after that. 75m is my main target right now, and then I want to reach 80m. It will require a lot of hard work, but I am sure I will be able to do it," he said.71.02m is not enough: A long way to goNirbhay knows that 71.02m is not enough to compete at the biggest international events. Even though his throw was above the Asian Games qualification mark of 69.12m, he missed the opportunity to compete at the Asian Games because of the timing of the qualification process and the deadlines involved."Practice was going on. The qualification issue was actually about dates. It depends on the host country. If the host sends an invitation or agrees to accommodate you, then things can be worked out, even if you are late. But there is a deadline for everything."There is a fixed time for it. By the time that deadline passed, I was not competing. I was only preparing for practice and other things. I had not even thought about whether I would go or not. We could not make a decision in time, so it did not happen. I could not go," he said.Nirbhay believes Indian hammer throw needs to improve its standards. While athletes in other events have raised their levels, he wants to bring the same change to hammer throw."I feel I can take hammer throw forward in India. We need to change things. Neeraj (Chopra) bhai has set an example for everyone in javelin. I want to do the same in hammer throw. He first crossed 70m, then 80m, 85m and now 90m. I want to achieve similar milestones in hammer throw," Nirbhay said."The standard of hammer throw in India has been very low for a long time. I want to raise that standard. I also want other athletes who are currently behind to reach that level. I want to see more youngsters take up hammer throw as a career and more athletes come into the event," he said.Nirbhay's Olympic dreamsIndia has never had an Olympic medal in hammer throw. The country has also had very few representatives in the event at the Games.Somnath Chopra represented India at the 1948 Summer Olympics and finished 23rd in the qualifying round. Erman Bastian represented India at the 1960 Summer Olympics but did not start his event.Praveen Kumar Sobti, who later became famous for playing Bheem in the television series Mahabharat, represented India at the 1968 Summer Olympics. He finished 20th in the qualifying round.India has won five medals in hammer throw at the Asian Games, including two silver and three bronze. Somnath Chopra and Kishen Singh won silver and bronze respectively at the 1951 Games. Praveen Kumar added another bronze in 1966, while Nirmal Singh Grewal won silver in 1974. Manju Bala was India's most recent hammer throw medallist, winning bronze at the 2014 Asian Games.India has won just one hammer throw medal in Commonwealth Games history. Praveen Kumar Sobti won silver at the 1966 Commonwealth Games in Kingston.For Nirbhay, breaking the national record is only the first step. He wants to take Indian hammer throw to a higher level and believes the country can win an Olympic medal in the event. The Olympic qualification mark for the 2028 Los Angeles Games is 78.50m."Why can't we win an Olympic medal? As I said, we need to set an example. I can be that example. I really want to put hammer throw on India's map of Olympic medal-winning events. India can win an Olympic medal in hammer throw. We just need one example, one athlete who achieves something big. After that, the path will become easier for others."Now I have almost all the facilities I need. I get support from the Athletics Federation and SAI. My coaches, including Naval Singh, have given their best. I have the equipment and everything else I need. So I will do it. I believe in myself. I will achieve this," he said.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: It is the responsibility of top athletes to look after the sports administration: Saina Nehwal
articles.summary: Pune: London Olympics bronze medallistshuttler Saina Nehwal feels involvement of former top athletes in the administrative roles can lift the standard of
articles.body: Pune: London Olympics bronze medallistshuttler Saina Nehwal feels involvement of former top athletes in the administrative roles can lift the standard of Indian sports.The shuttler, who has won the Sportspersons of Outstanding Merit (SOM) election of the Indian Olympic Association (IOA) polls, saids she feels the need to give it back to the sport. “It is a very good sign that sports is now being looked after by people who have played at the highest level. A lot of knowledge can be shared among these sportspersons, who come from different disciplines. Whatever knowledge I have gained from badminton, I will be able to share with theathletes, and similarly, I can learn from their experiences. We can collectively discuss what is required to build more champions and strengthen the sporting system in India,” she told TOI.“We have the Commonwealth Games coming up, and we are also looking at hosting the Olympics. Having experienced sportspersons in sports administration will only help improve our results and medal tally,” she said.Saina has won an Olympic medal and has recently retired from active badminton. She feels staying in touch with the sport makes it better for the administrators to understand the need of the sport better.“As you grow older, you begin to understand what it takes to make a champion and what all is required to achieve that. When I look at countries such as China and Korea, I notice that their sports associations are often headed by people who have themselves performed at the highest level and won Olympic medals. I strongly believe that experienced sportspersons who have performed at the highest level should be involved in every aspect of sports administration. They understand what is happening on the ground and what athletes actually need. They travel extensively with players and understand the challenges they face.”On the possibility of her contesting for the post of the president, she said, “I don't know. Whether it is me or any other sportsperson, it hardly matters. What matters is that we work together to improve Indian sport and increase our medal tally. We should aim to reach the level of countries such as China and America.The position of president or any other post will obviously have a name associated with it. But ultimately, the important thing is how we work together and what we can collectively achieve to win more medals for the country.”Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Olympic champion Emily Craig says her passion is art
articles.summary: Emily Craig from Pembury, who became an Olympic champion in 2024, says she loves her life now.
articles.body:
Hanging artwork inside a fine art gallery near Leicester Square is not where you would expect to find a reigning Olympic champion.

Emily Craig, 33, won gold with Imogen Grant in the lightweight double skull event in Paris, dubbed the "last ever" champions, with the discipline now removed from the Olympic programme.

Imogen continues to row, hoping to reach LA in a higher weight class, but Emily, who is from Pembury, now works in the art world.

"I definitely don't regret it," she says. "I love my life now.

"This was always my plan and I'd done a lot of prep mentally and emotionally.

"But the result definitely helped, the itch was scratched."

In Paris, she met Rolling Stone Mick Jagger, and has since met King Charles III, been invited to the Royal Box at Wimbledon, and attended numerous film premieres.

Emily said she had given herself six months to enjoy being Olympic Champion, before turning her attention to a career in art, something she has always wanted.

She had considered retirement after the Tokyo Olympics, where she came fourth, with Imogen, missing out on a medal by 0.001 second.

"I couldn't really walk away with that being my last result," she said.

"But I went back with the mind that I would be retiring after Paris."

Emily did a history of art degree, and a masters in East-Asian art, before "handing in my dissertation and becoming a professional athlete for 10 years".

She had hoped for a "fairy tale" finish in Tokyo, but says Paris was a "very suitable place for an art lover to win gold".

Even while training, Emily did work experience "here and there", and her first job since retirement was photographing coins.

Now at Darnley Fine Art, she said: "I know there's a lot I don't know, and I very much came to this role willing to learn and to see where it takes me."

Though she has no regrets, searching for an entry-level job in her 30s has not always been easy, even for an Olympic Champion.

She added: "There's definitely been points in the job search when things weren't quite going so well.

"I wondered if anyone was ever going to see me as anything other than an athlete.

"In general though I've put the work into planning retirement and it's paid off, and I'd very much encourage other athletes that there is a life beyond sport."

articles.title: Tatjana Smith switch to Netherlands sad - Swimming South Africa CEO Zikie Molusi
articles.summary: Tatjana Smith's decision to switch allegiance to the Netherlands is "sad" for South Africa, says the head of the nation's swimming federation.
articles.body:
The decision by South Africa's most decorated Olympian Tatjana Smith to switch allegiance to the Netherlands is "sad" for the nation, says Swimming South Africa CEO Zikie Molusi.

Double Olympic champion Smith, who has dual citizenship because her father is Dutch, was in tears when she announced her decision on Wednesday.

She said that the opportunity "offers greater high-performance support" and that South African athletes "deserve a system that gives them an opportunity to thrive, not just survive".

"When I received that correspondence from Tatjana we understood because she has been really generous and kind enough to articulate the rationale that informed the decision," Molusi, the acting CEO of the governing body, told eNews Channel Africa.

"A very sad decision for the country, particularly as we were preparing to take the team to Beijing for the short course World Championships in December."

Tearful Smith switches allegiance to Netherlands

Smith, formerly Schoenmaker, previously said financial worries, which included a dispute with Swimming South Africa over prize money, contributed to her decision to step away from the sport after the Paris 2024 Olympics.

The 29-year-old, who has won four Olympic medals, came out of retirement in September and is set to represent the Netherlands for the first time at the World Championships from 1-6 December.

Smith said representing the Netherlands would give her "the potential to build a more sustainable career".

She said the "financial and practical challenges of swimming were among the reasons my previous career became difficult to sustain".

Speaking to Radio 702, Molusi accepted that Swimming South Africa should not have withheld prize money from Smith following the 2023 World Championships.

Molusi said that was caused by conflicting sponsorship agreements but it "shouldn't have happened".

Of the 21 athletes competing for South Africa at the Worlds next month, Molusi said "probably 50% will be subsidised fully", with the rest receiving partial support.

"It's an ecosystem issue within South African sport that possibly needs to be dealt with," Molusi said.

"This comes as a result of the inadequate funding that sport federations are receiving."

articles.title: Plata de la windsurfista Olivia Sánchez en los Juegos Olímpicos de la Juventud
articles.standfirst: Décima medalla de España en la penúltima jornada de competición en Dakar
articles.summary: Décima medalla de España en la penúltima jornada de competición en Dakar
articles.body: España ha elevado a dos dígitos su número de medallas en los Juegos Olímpicos de la Juventud que se disputan en Dakar (Senegal). Lo ha hecho en la penúltima jornada de competición merced a la plata de la windsurfista Olivia Sánchez, que ha acabado empatada a puntos (24) con la ganadora del oro, la italiana Laura Grasso. La sevillana de 15 años ha estado toda la competición en los puestos delanteros, ganando dos de las 14 regatas disputadas. La cancelación de la 15ª y definitiva regata en Saly Beach West le ha impedido luchar por la victoria, a la que también aspiraba la china Ziyan Wu, finalmente tercera a tres puntos de la española y la transalpina. Este nuevo éxito de la deportista del Club Náutico Sevilla se suma a sus dos títulos mundiales y dos europeos en categoría sub-15, y a su bronce en el Campeonato del Mundo Techno Sub-17 del pasado mes de abril en Turquía. En la jornada final de este viernes, España tiene asegurada una medalla más, gracias a las chicas del balonmano playa, y luchará por la duodécima en el siempre espectacular breaking. La selección española juvenil femenina de balonmano playa disputará este viernes la final después de derrotar hoy a Senegal por 2-1 en una emocionante semifinal resuelta en los shoot-outs. Su rival en la lucha por el oro será Uruguay, que en la otra semifinal venció a Francia. Además, la representante españolas en breakin, Mini Ali, se ha metido en cuartos tras ganar hoy sus tres 'batallas' a la alemana Melkez, la marroquí Nawel y la surcoreana Minji. Su primera rival mañana en cuartos será la francesa Queen Lolita, y si gana se meterá en la lucha por los metales.

articles.title: PT Usha enters IOA presidential race again, files nomination through Ice Hockey Federation
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: The Indian Olympic Association (IOA) presidential election has taken a fresh turn, with incumbent president PT Usha entering the fray again
articles.body: NEW DELHI: The Indian Olympic Association (IOA) presidential election has taken a fresh turn, with incumbent president PT Usha entering the fray again after appearing to be virtually out of contention following her defeat in the Sportspersons of Outstanding Merit (SOMs) election.Usha has filed her nomination through the Ice Hockey Association of India, potentially setting up another contest for the IOA president's post. Her candidature could bring her into direct competition with candidates backed by sections of the National Sports Federations (NSFs) and the sports administration.Usha's return to the presidential race comes in the aftermath of the SOM election, where four prominent former athletes – world championships medallist Anju Bobby George, London Olympics medallist Saina Nehwal, former India archer Dola Banerjee and former hockey captain Rani Rampal – came together against her. Their collective position, coupled with last-minute withdrawals, resulted in Usha losing the contest.The developments surrounding the SOM election had also triggered allegations against several individuals, including members of the IOA executive committee, with claims of interference from sections of the sports administration. Usha has written to the International Olympic Committee (IOC), raising concerns over the manner in which the SOM election was conducted.Her nomination through the Ice Hockey Association of India now puts her back in contention, although it remains to be seen how much support she can garner from the federations and other stakeholders.Meanwhile, former Athletics Federation of India (AFI) president Adille Sumariwalla has returned as the federation's representative after withdrawing from the SOM election. Hockey India representative Bhola Nath Singh and All India Tennis Association (AITA) representative Chintan Parekh are among the other notable names in the latest list.Rohit Rajpal, who is part of the IOA executive committee, is not among the representatives in the latest list.The developments also come ahead of India's presentation on its proposed bid to host the 2036 Olympic Games, scheduled for November 26.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates.
